Getting Started with TypeScript - Part 1

January 10, 2024 by Test Author 1 min read

Introduction

Welcome to the first part of our TypeScript Fundamentals series! In this series, we'll cover everything you need to know to get started with TypeScript.

What is TypeScript?

TypeScript is a typed superset of JavaScript that compiles to plain JavaScript. It adds optional static typing and class-based object-oriented programming to the language.

Why TypeScript?

  • Type Safety: Catch errors at compile time
  • Better IDE Support: Enhanced autocomplete and refactoring
  • Modern JavaScript: Use the latest JavaScript features
  • Scalability: Better for large codebases
// Example: Type annotations
let message: string = "Hello, TypeScript!";
let count: number = 42;
let isActive: boolean = true;

function greet(name: string): string {
  return `Hello, ${name}!`;
}

Next Steps

In the next part, we'll dive into TypeScript's type system and explore interfaces and types.
